title: End-to-end classroom project
goal: Clean, audit, summarize, visualize, and export a small dataset with an explanation of every choice.
prerequisites: Core modules and plotting; keep raw and clean data distinct.

cells.title: Clean the raw table and keep an audit trail
cells.explanation: Bring the cleaning skills together. Remove the known exact duplicate, normalize labels, preserve why a score is unavailable, and flag impossible attendance as missing. This exercise makes no assumption that an absent score equals zero.
cells.code:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

print(df[["Student_ID", "Name", "Campus", "Score", "Score_Status", "Attendance"]])
print("Rows:", len(df))
print("Unavailable scores:", df["Score"].isna().sum())

questions.prompt: Why is Score_Status created before numeric conversion?
questions.answer: The original text distinguishes an absent student from an already missing score. Conversion alone would erase that distinction.

questions.prompt: How many rows and missing numeric scores remain?
questions.answer: 12 unique students remain; two scores are missing numerically, S004 and S008.

questions.prompt: Why not replace attendance 105 with 100 automatically?
questions.answer: The correct attendance is unknown. Capping would invent a value; flagging allows later correction from a source.

cells.task: Use the cleaned table to create a review list containing students with a missing Score, Study_Hours, or Attendance. Store it in result with columns Student_ID, Score, Study_Hours, and Attendance, then print result.
cells.hint: Use isna().any(axis=1) across the three columns.
cells.solution:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

review_columns = ["Score", "Study_Hours", "Attendance"]
result = df.loc[df[review_columns].isna().any(axis=1), ["Student_ID"] + review_columns]
print(result)
cells.solution_note: Review S004, S006, S008, and S011. Each record has at least one unavailable or invalid value. A review flag does not tell you how the missing value should be replaced.

check.prompt: What evidence supports changing 105 to missing?
options: Attendance is defined as a percentage from 0 to 100
Every high value is an outlier to remove
Pandas does not support numbers above 100
check.feedback: The column's documented range makes 105 invalid. Pandas itself has no such numeric limit.

cells.verify:
assert len(df) == 12
assert df['Student_ID'].is_unique
assert df['Score'].isna().sum() == 2
assert df['Attendance'].isna().sum() == 1
cells.watch: Do not discard the raw labels before you have recorded their meaning.
cells.takeaway: Clean with documented rules and preserve the reasons for missing values.

cells.title: Report a mean with its denominator
cells.explanation: A group average is easier to interpret when its sample count is visible. Count all students and count recorded scores separately. Pandas mean skips missing numeric scores by default; say that in your report.
cells.code:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

result = (df.groupby("Campus", as_index=False)
          .agg(Students=("Student_ID", "size"),
               Recorded_Scores=("Score", "count"),
               Mean_Score=("Score", "mean")))
print(result.round(2))

questions.prompt: How are Students and Recorded_Scores different?
questions.answer: Students counts rows. Recorded_Scores counts non-missing scores.

questions.prompt: Which campus has fewer recorded scores than students?
questions.answer: Dubai has six students but only four recorded scores in the cleaned raw table.

questions.prompt: May you report the mean as an average of all six Dubai students?
questions.answer: No. It is based on four recorded scores. The missing observations may also affect the interpretation.

cells.task: Produce the same report by Program. Add Missing_Scores = Students - Recorded_Scores, then sort from highest to lowest Mean_Score.
cells.hint: Use groupby('Program'), named aggregation, and a new column.
cells.solution:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

result = (df.groupby("Program", as_index=False)
          .agg(Students=("Student_ID", "size"),
               Recorded_Scores=("Score", "count"),
               Mean_Score=("Score", "mean")))
result["Missing_Scores"] = result["Students"] - result["Recorded_Scores"]
result = result.sort_values("Mean_Score", ascending=False)
print(result.round(2))
cells.solution_note: AI has six recorded scores and a mean of 85.83. IT has four recorded scores, two missing scores, and a mean of 77.25. These fictional data do not establish a general difference between programs.

check.prompt: Which denominator does mean use here?
options: Every row, treating missing values as zero
Only non-missing score values in each group
check.feedback: mean skips missing numeric values by default. Reporting count beside it makes the denominator clear.

cells.solution_verify:
assert result['Program'].tolist() == ['AI','IT']
assert result['Missing_Scores'].tolist() == [0,2]
assert np.isclose(result.iloc[0]['Mean_Score'],515/6)
assert np.isclose(result.iloc[1]['Mean_Score'],77.25)
cells.watch: A polished mean without the number of observed values can mislead.
cells.takeaway: Attach counts and missingness to summary statistics.

cells.title: Join, audit, and select a follow-up list
cells.explanation: Combine the cleaned records with assessment results, checking both match quality and row counts. The follow-up rule below uses an observed Score under 75 or a missing assessment. Unknown scores need separate review, not automatic failure.
cells.code:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

joined = df.merge(assessment(), on="Student_ID", how="left",
                  validate="one_to_one", indicator=True)
mask = joined["Score"].lt(75).fillna(False) | joined["_merge"].eq("left_only")
result = joined.loc[mask, ["Student_ID", "Score", "Quiz", "_merge"]]
print(result)

questions.prompt: Why is fillna(False) used in the score condition?
questions.answer: An unknown score should not be classified as below 75. Missing scores are handled by a separate review process.

questions.prompt: Which student is selected because an assessment is missing?
Does excluding an unknown score mean the student passed?
questions.answer: No. It only means this specific rule does not classify that student. Missing data still need review.

cells.task: Create a separate audit with an outer merge. Show only unmatched IDs and whether each ID belongs to the student table or the assessment table.
cells.solution:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

audit = df.merge(assessment(), on="Student_ID", how="outer",
                 validate="one_to_one", indicator=True)
result = audit.loc[audit["_merge"].ne("both"), ["Student_ID", "_merge"]]

cells.solution_note: S012 is student-only; S013 is assessment-only. Investigate both before treating the assessment file as complete.

check.prompt: A missing score should automatically become a failing score.
options: False; a documented rule or source correction is needed
check.feedback: A missing observation is not an observed zero or a confirmed failure.

cells.watch: A missing comparison may propagate pd.NA; decide how the rule treats unknowns.
cells.takeaway: Keep classification rules separate from data-quality review.

cells.title: Create a table, a plot, and a reproducible export
cells.explanation: Finish with a compact report and a plot that answers a stated question. Keep the clean table and the summary as separate outputs. On a new run, rebuild the report from the source and the written cleaning rules.
cells.code:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

result = df.pivot_table(index="Campus", columns="Program", values="Score",
                        aggfunc="mean", observed=True)
counts = df.pivot_table(index="Campus", columns="Program", values="Score",
                        aggfunc="count", observed=True)
print("Recorded mean scores:")
print(result.round(2))
print("Recorded score counts:")
print(counts)
ax = result.plot.bar(color=["#216b62", "#b58b45"], rot=0)
ax.set_title("Recorded mean score by campus and program")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean score (0–100)")
ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
df.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "capstone_cleaned_students.csv", index=False)
result.round(2).to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "capstone_score_summary.csv")
counts.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "capstone_recorded_counts.csv")
print("Saved cleaned data, summary, and recorded counts in outputs/.")

questions.prompt: Why does the summary CSV keep its index?
questions.answer: Campus is stored in the pivot table index and carries meaning. Removing it would lose the campus labels.

questions.prompt: How many mean values appear in this 2-by-2 table?
questions.answer: Four: AI and IT within Dubai and RAK.

questions.prompt: What must accompany this chart in a report?
questions.answer: The number of recorded scores per group, the missing-score policy, and a note that these are fictional teaching data. Bar differences do not prove causation.

cells.task: Make a Program-level report with columns Program, Recorded_Scores, and Mean_Score. Export it without a DataFrame index to capstone_program_report.csv. Read the exported file back into read_back and verify its columns and row count.
cells.hint: Use groupby, agg, to_csv(index=False), and read_csv.
cells.solution:
df = raw_students().drop_duplicates().copy()
df["Name"] = df["Name"].astype("string").str.strip()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].astype("string").str.strip().str.title()
df["Campus"] = df["Campus"].replace({"Rak": "RAK"})
df["Score_Status"] = "recorded"
df.loc[df["Score"].isna(), "Score_Status"] = "missing"
df.loc[df["Score"].eq("absent"), "Score_Status"] = "absent"
df["Score"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Score"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Study_Hours"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Study_Hours"], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
df["Attendance"] = df["Attendance"].astype("Float64")
df.loc[~df["Attendance"].between(0, 100), "Attendance"] = pd.NA
df["Join_Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Join_Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

result = (df.groupby("Program", as_index=False)
          .agg(Recorded_Scores=("Score", "count"), Mean_Score=("Score", "mean")))
result["Mean_Score"] = result["Mean_Score"].round(2)
path = OUTPUT_DIR / "capstone_program_report.csv"
result.to_csv(path, index=False)
read_back = pd.read_csv(path)
print(read_back)
print("Columns preserved:", read_back.columns.tolist() == result.columns.tolist())
cells.solution_note: The CSV contains Program, Recorded_Scores, and Mean_Score, with no extra unnamed index column. Reading the file back checks the delivered table, not just the in-memory object.

check.prompt: When is index=False appropriate for this Program report?
options: When all meaningful labels already live in columns
check.feedback: This report has Program as a normal column. Its default numeric index adds no useful information to the CSV.

cells.solution_verify:
assert read_back.columns.tolist() == ['Program','Recorded_Scores','Mean_Score']
assert read_back['Recorded_Scores'].sum() == 10
assert read_back.shape == (2,3)
cells.watch: CSV does not preserve every pandas dtype. Recheck dtypes when loading it later.
cells.takeaway: Deliver a report that another person can reproduce and interpret.
